title: records-of-truth-carry-one-extension-artifact
intention: Every record of truth carries one extension, .artifact, so that 'is this a record?' is answerable from the filename alone and the jurisdiction, the PreToolUse gate and the commit question each collapse to one rule instead of a list of directories and basenames.
why: Law 1 (one spelling of the record set instead of a directory list re-derived by three readers), Law 4 (the deny rule becomes one line of physics — Akien: 'then we only disallow one extension'), Law 6 (the door stays the one gate; the rename is its first bulk write and proves it under load)
how: The rename is the door's first bulk write: `cairn artifact rename` per record through the door (old path absent, new path chained), readers rewritten behind a both-extensions flag first, rehearsed in a scratch clone, then one journaled act per repo committed under the hook; jurisdiction.json and bin/cmd/artifactgate collapse to one *.artifact rule; the flag is removed last.
falsifier: DONE when, measured by cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_artifact_rename.py and the live corpus: (1) zero files under CairnCommons/{tickets,troubles,decisions,slates,ideas,questions,adjudications} end in .json, and zero state/history/intention+why/validation files under cairn end in .json (find + count, both zero); (2) jurisdiction.json carries one rule per root — {"name": "*.artifact"} — and locate() answers yes for every renamed file and no for the lab, node_classes, notes; (3) both journals verify from genesis with every rename journaled (old path's last entry absent, new path chained from it) and `cairn artifact check` passes both roots; (4) every reader in the 127-file / 322-site census (measured 2026-09-13) reads .artifact: the ticket inspector, the harbor's clearance, the review queue, the session-open banner, the chart doors, the sorted/saveslate/idea doors all run green on the renamed corpus; (5) a Write/Edit/Bash redirect aimed at any *.artifact is refused at PreToolUse by one extension check. WRONG INTENT if a reader outside our repos needs .json — then the extension carried information and the rule is a directory rule. HORIZON: the outside-readers census is the first piece; if it reds, this ticket routes back before any file moves.
traces_to: Law 1 (one spelling of the record set instead of a directory list re-derived by three readers), Law 4 (the deny rule becomes one line of physics — Akien: 'then we only disallow one extension'), Law 6 (the door stays the one gate; the rename is its first bulk write and proves it under load)
